function: Multi-agent TD3 learns RIS phase shifts jointly with user transmit powers, time allocation, and task-split coefficient, to maximize secrecy capacity over energy in RIS-aided MEC (p. 5-6).
system: Uplink NOMA, two single-antenna users and one single-antenna eavesdropper, BS with M=4 antennas, passive reflecting RIS with N=16 or 64 elements; band not stated (p. 3, 9).
method: Multi-agent TD3 (centralized training, decentralized execution) with user, RIS, and MEC agents, each with actor and critic networks of three layers, Leaky ReLU; reinforcement learning (p. 7, 9).
data_channel: Custom simulated Rician channel with Rayleigh NLoS, 30 dB path loss at 1 m, path-loss exponents 3 to 3.5, generated in MATLAB; no dataset (p. 8-9).
test_conditions: Training and evaluation on the same simulated setup per curve, over episodes; separate runs for N=16/64, with/without RIS, fixed/optimized alpha, jamming; no unseen test (p. 10-12).
baselines: Learned only: MADDPG, single-agent TD3, single-agent DDPG; ablations with fixed alpha and without RIS; no non-learned method compared (p. 10-11).
metrics: Secrecy capacity, total energy consumption, average reward (secrecy capacity over energy), critic loss (p. 10-11).
complexity: Training complexity order O(Nepisodes*Nsteps*NB*sum of el*el+1) from layer widths; no FLOPs or runtime reported (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 9: "stand for the LoS component and Rayleigh fading component, respectively, and K is the Rician factor". The channel is the authors' own Rician model with a 30 dB reference loss (Eq. 42); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 12: "the eavesdropper transmits a White Gaussian Interference Signal in each training episode", so the jamming case is trained, not tested on unseen data; p. 9: the network is resized for each N. All results are training-episode curves; no trained model is tested on an unseen condition.
q3_support: p. 10: "compared with both the MADDPG method and the single-agent algorithms" (Figs. 5-7: MADDPG, single-agent TD3, DDPG) gives learned baselines only. The without-RIS and fixed-alpha curves (p. 11) are variants of the proposed scheme; no non-learned method (random or fixed RIS, AO) is compared.
q4_support: p. 8: "Summing up, the total computational complexity is" O(Nepisodes Nsteps NB sum el el+1), the order of the training cost (Sec. III-C); FLOPs and runtime are not reported.
q5_support: p. 9: "is simulated by MATLAB R2020a". The channel is generated from Eq. 42 and no code or data link or DOI is given anywhere in the paper, nor is a public channel dataset used.
notes: Title on page 1 is 'Security Enhancement for RIS-Aided MEC Systems With Deep Reinforcement Learning' with DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2024.3476139, so the PDF matches. Included through the rule that a work learning a physical-layer decision jointly with one above it passes above_phy: the RIS agent outputs the phase shifts (state and action, p. 6) together with offloading variables (alpha, time allocation, power). Area 3 for the RIS phase shifts; the goal is secrecy capacity, a physical-layer security objective that is not an excluded function (authentication, anti-jamming). The BS receive beamformer w appears in problem (26) but not in the action space (p. 6) and how it is set is not stated. Tables I-III were read from the page images (pages 3 and 9); no carrier frequency is given.
